newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota seeks NYSE listing by 2000 -- newspaper.
newsitem.headline: Toyota seeks NYSE listing by 2000 -- newspaper.

text.p: Toyota Motor Corp wants to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange by 2000, a Japanese newspaper reported on Tuesday.
The mass-circulation daily Yomiuri Shimbun quoted Toyota's president, Hiroshi Okuda, as saying in an interview that it hopes to list its shares in New York by 2000 to improve its global image.

"The issue of disclosure would be difficult," Okuda was quoted as saying. But he added: "We have already reached an internal consensus that doing so is necessary for the purpose of our public relations. We hope to be listed by 2000."

Toyota would come under strict scrutiny from the Securities Exchange Commission (SEC) and would need to win the body's approval for the listing. Toyota aims to set up a special team within the company soon to prepare the financial data needed for the listing, the newspaper said.
Toyota has set 2000 as the target year for the listing because the company believes it will be able to show itself to be a global company to overseas investors by that time, the newspaper said.
Toyota is due to complete its current plan for expanding overseas production in 1997 and is looking to expand output in China and India by 2000.
A Toyota official was not immediately available for comment on the newspaper interview.
